it's left behind a lot of damage. More than 600,000 homes lost power at the
storm's height. There were also four storm-related deaths. In Montgomery,
Alabama, Mayor Steve Reid was grateful that problems there from the hurricane
were not as severe as expected. We avoided the worst of the storm and we're
blessed certainly in our city, but I just want to thank all the first responders
and all the people who helped us in the days and hours leading up to it, as well

killed in hundreds wounded in an attack by Yemen's Houthi militia on Saudi
Arabia's main airport, and Piers Chandelis Duster reports. The Saudi
Silver Aviation Authority says at least a dozen people are dead and more than 300
are injured after an attack on King Khalid International Airport on
Saturday. A U.S. citizen was also killed in the attack, according to Secretary of
State Marco Rubio. It's the deadliest attack on a Gulf Arab country since the
U.S. and Israel launched a war with Iran in February. The Iranian-backed Houthis
claimed responsibility. The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh urged all U.S. citizens to
avoid the airport and surrounding areas. Secretary Rubio said the "reprehensible
attacks demonstrate a blatant disregard for innocent civilian life." He also said
the attacks must stop now. President Trump told reporters early Saturday the
U.S. would make a decision soon on whether to intervene against the Houthis.
Chandelis Duster, NPR News. The FDA says it won't finish internal research on the
abortion pill Myphopristone until March. As NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin reports,
several Republican-run states have filed lawsuits. Over a hundred studies have
shown that Myphopristone is safe and effective in ending a pregnancy in its
first 10 weeks. It's been approved by the FDA for more than 25 years, and the
agency says it's been used by more than 7.5 million patients. Currently, the FDA
allows it to be prescribed remotely and sent through the mail. Anti-abortion
rights groups and some state and federal Republican officials have been pushing
hard for the FDA to restrict access nationally, including through court
cases. FDA announced last year it would review its safety data. The agency told a
judge in one of the Myphopristone cases this week that March is the earliest the
report would be ready. Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News. Police in
Pennsylvania say a man killed eight people late Friday night at his home in
Erie before taking his own life. Among those killed were a pregnant woman and
several children. Police say the man was related to seven of the people he killed.
Authorities in India have begun a major crackdown in New Delhi. They've detained
thousands of protesters from the so-called cockroach movement, which
intended to hold a mass demonstration there. The group is campaigning against
a controversial voter registration list revision that has caused anger at the
government. You're listening to NPR News. Panama's government has declared a
state of emergency after two powerful earthquakes hit that country on Friday.
The quake's had magnitudes of 7.7 and 6.6. They caused damage in all 10 of the
country's provinces, as well as two indigenous territories. So far no deaths
have been reported, but there have been a number of injuries along with
significant structural damage. Officials say the Panama Canal remains
operational. Authorities in Poland have arrested a woman suspected of injuring
three people at a school in Warsaw. As Esme Nicholson reports, this is the third
such attack across the country this week. Police say the 21-year-old woman used a
dangerous object to attack a 17-year-old girl, whom they believe the suspect did
not know. Authorities have not confirmed whether this incident is related to two
knife attacks at other schools on Wednesday and Thursday this week. In the
wake of these separate attacks, police say they detained 76 people across Poland
and sent officers to check nearly 50,000 schools. Authorities say despite media
reports about concerns this could be a social media challenge, they have no
evidence of that. They say extra security measures at schools such as bad checks
will continue. For NPR News, I'm Esme Nicholson in Berlin.
Patry Gyarho and Eva Navarro scored in the first 14 minutes and Spain never
looked back as they beat the U.S. women's soccer team Saturday 2-0. The two teams
will now meet once again outside Philadelphia on Tuesday. Spain and the
U.S. have combined to win the last three World Cups. The Cleveland Guardians beat
the Chicago White Sox Saturday 2-0 to complete a comeback from an 0-2
deficit to win the American League Division Series. I'm Dale Willman and
you're listening to NPR News. This message comes from NetSuite. AI is
